text_blocks.snippet: The COVID-19 virus is generally considered contagious from 2 days before the onset of symptoms until 10 days after symptoms first appear.
snippet_highlighted_words: 2 days before the onset of symptoms until 10 days after symptoms first appear

list.title: 2 days before symptom onset:
list.snippet: The virus can be transmitted from infected individuals even before they show symptoms.

list.title: 10 days after symptom onset:
list.snippet: Most people will no longer be contagious after 10 days, even if they still have mild symptoms.

list.title: 24 hours after symptoms improve:
list.snippet: If symptoms improve significantly within 24 hours, the individual may be considered no longer contagious.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that these are general guidelines, and the contagious period may vary depending on factors such as the individual's immune system, the severity of their infection, and the specific variant of the virus.

list.snippet: People who are asymptomatic or have very mild symptoms may be contagious for longer periods.
Individuals who test positive on a rapid antigen test should isolate themselves for at least 5 days, regardless of symptoms.
People who test positive on a PCR test should isolate themselves until they receive a negative result, even if they are asymptomatic.
